name: BAS Box Handling Experiment
disclaimer: This is a CUSTOM PROTOTYPE experiment designed for the SIH 2026 prototype, INSPIRED BY ISRO Problem Statement 26174. The official publicly available description is truncated after 'You are given a box that contains two smaller boxes of color red and yellow...', so the 7-step sequence below is OUR OWN demonstration sequence and is NOT the official ISRO sequence. It exists only to develop and validate a local activity-recognition + sequence-validation prototype.
description: An astronaut approaches the experiment area, opens the main experiment box (which contains one red box and one yellow box), then picks each box up and places it into the designated target area. The experiment is complete once both boxes are correctly placed.

evidenceNotes.PRESENT: the class was detected this run (arrival edge, not a per-frame latch)
evidenceNotes.MOVED: the tracked class was displaced over consecutive frames (one episode per physical motion)
evidenceNotes.PLACED: the tracked class came to rest inside the target area after a confirmed motion (one episode per placement)
evidenceNotes.KNOWN_LIMITS: APPROACH is presence only - it does not prove proximity to the box. OPEN_BOX is grounded on the first MOTION OF A STORED BOX (red or yellow) because no container or lid detector exists in any shipped model; opening the box jiggling its contents is credited as that move, and it is a genuine inference, not a measurement. HAND_NEAR_* is unavailable (no hand-landmark model installed), so a PICK is proven by object motion only - 'held by the astronaut' is not verified. Because OPEN_BOX consumes the first content-move episode, PICK_RED/PICK_YELLOW each require a NEW, separate motion episode. PLACE_* additionally needs a target area, and NO shipped detector can see one (the custom model knows only red/yellow, yolov8n is COCO, the heuristic sees person/red/yellow): the destination is fixed station hardware, so its region is supplied by the ACTIVITY_TARGET_AREA config (x1,y1,x2,y2 normalized 0-1) rather than perceived. With that unset the run is honest about it - status reports targetAreaSource=none and placedGrounded=false, and PLACED is never claimed.

steps.description: The main experiment box is opened so the red and yellow boxes inside become reachable.

steps.voiceInstruction: confirm both boxes are in the target area
steps.description: Both the red and yellow box are inside the target area. Terminal step - the experiment finishes.

validationRules.nextExpectedOnError: unchanged - the offending step must be performed again to advance
validationRules.skippedStepEvidence: SKIPPED_STEP is advisory and is emitted together with OUT_OF_SEQUENCE / WRONG_OBJECT / WRONG_SEQUENCE; progress advances exclusively on STEP_MATCHED
validationRules.recourseRefinement: a later-than-expected detection is refined to WRONG_OBJECT when the expected and observed steps share an action but differ in object (e.g. PICK_RED expected, PICK_YELLOW observed) and to WRONG_SEQUENCE when they share an object but differ in action (e.g. PLACE_RED before PICK_RED); steps without action/object metadata always stay OUT_OF_SEQUENCE

errorTypes.when: detected activity equals the expected step
known activity from a later step is detected before the expected step, with no shared action or object to refine it
the same action is performed on a different object than the expected step requires (e.g. PICK_YELLOW while PICK_RED is expected)
the expected object is acted on with the wrong action (e.g. PLACE_RED before the red box was picked up)
advisory emitted together with OUT_OF_SEQUENCE / WRONG_OBJECT / WRONG_SEQUENCE (a later step implies earlier steps were skipped)
known activity from an already-completed step is detected again
detected activity is null or not defined in this experiment
detected activity confidence is below the validationRules.lowConfidenceThreshold
errorTypes.progressEffect: none - treat the detection as uncertain

example.note: The expected step does not change when a later step fires out of order; the operator (or voice cue) re-prompts for the expected step.
